subject: Throughput sizing follow-up — FinEx SLOs & next steps

Subject: Throughput sizing follow-up — FinEx SLOs & next steps

Hi Alex — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can size a recommended configuration: 

Summary of what we heard
- Target P95 tail latency for generate API: 250–300ms (customer-driven).
- Streaming required for progressive responses (partial tokens to client).
- Typical prompt size: ~60 tokens. Expected generated tokens per response: ~150.
- Steady-state QPS estimated: ~80–100 requests/sec. Peak (marketing events, batch jobs): up to ~500–600 QPS for short bursts.
- Concurrency: 40–60 steady concurrent users, bursts up to 400–600 concurrent requests during spikes.

Clarifying questions (can you confirm?):
1) Are the average/median request sizes above accurate, or do you have a distribution (P50/P90 token lengths)?
2) Do peaks happen predictably (scheduled batch) or as unplanned user-driven spikes?
3) Any hard SLOs we should treat as blockers (e.g., P95 < 200ms)?

Next steps / ask from FinEx by EOW if possible:
- Share a representative traffic profile (CSV/JSON) with timestamps, tokens per request, and QPS by minute.
- Confirm whether streaming must provide interleaved partial outputs for all requests.

Attached is a quick sizing worksheet (finex_sizing_template.xlsx) — fill in the traffic_profile section and drop it back here. Rafael and Marissa from our infra/perf team are cc'd and will propose an initial capacity plan based on what you share.

Happy to hop on a 30-min follow-up if that helps. Proposed times: Mon 11/8 10:00am PT or Tue 11/9 11:00am PT.

Thanks,
Neha

Hi Neha — thanks for the clear recap. See answers below and I attached a short traffic profile export (traffic_profile_20261104.json).

Answers:
- Token distribution: median prompt size ~55 tokens, median response ~140 tokens. P90 total tokens/request ~420 (large contextual requests).
- Peak pattern: Mix — mostly user-driven spikes (product launches) but we also have scheduled nightly batch jobs (short windows, 5–15 minutes) that produce predictable bursts.
- SLOs: P95 target = 250ms for non-batched interactive traffic. For batch jobs we can accept higher latency but still want throughput guarantees.
- Streaming: yes — we require streaming for interactive chat use cases (clients render partial tokens as they arrive). For batch jobs we use non-streaming (longer responses ok).

Traffic numbers (last 30 days average & peaks):
- Steady-state interactive QPS: 75–95
- Typical concurrent interactive users: 35–55
- Burst peaks: up to 575 QPS observed during last launch (sustained ~7 minutes)
- Batch job peak: ~650 QPS for 10 minutes (single region)
- Average tokens per interaction (prompt + response): ~200 tokens

Attaching: traffic_profile_20261104.json (anonymized minute-level QPS + avg tokens).

We can meet Mon 11/8 10:00am PT. Please include Rafael and anyone from infra/serving who will own the capacity recommendations.

Thanks,

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Nov 2026 08:05:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Throughput sizing follow-up — Pre-call notes

Quick notes / initial thoughts before the 10am call with FinEx: 

- Based on avg 200 tokens/request and P95 target 250ms with streaming for interactive flows, we'll rely on low-latency kernels + continuous batching. Streaming increases memory/KV cache considerations — we should prioritize models with efficient autoregressive kernels (quantized FP16-friendly where possible).
- Ballpark initial config (single-region):
  - Interactive pool: 2x A100 80GB (reserved) + autoscale to 4 during sustained peaks, concurrency tuned ~8–16 streams/GPU depending on effective tokens/sec per request.
  - Batch pool: separate preemptible GPU pool (cost-optimized) for scheduled jobs to avoid head-of-line blocking.
  - Batching & caching: enable prefix KV cache for common prompts; target batch sizes that keep P95 under 250ms (we'll simulate).

Capacity calc notes (rough):
- If average request generates 200 tokens and effective generation throughput is 300 tokens/sec per GPU under our runtime for the chosen model, that's ~1.5 requests/sec/GPU (no batching). With batching we can raise that to ~10–12 req/sec/GPU while keeping latency targets (depends on prompt distribution).
- For FinEx steady ~85 QPS we likely need a minimum of 6–8 GPU-equivalent capacity in interactive pool when tuned for batching + streaming. Peaks to ~650 QPS will need autoscale headroom or a multi-variant fallback (smaller faster model) to preserve SLOs.

Questions to confirm on the call:
- Percent of traffic that strictly needs streaming vs can be non-streaming (this affects batching strategy).
- Expected per-request variance on token generation (how many >400 tokens?).
- Are cross-region fallbacks acceptable if single-region saturates?

I'll capture these in the sizing doc and bring a short spreadsheet to the call. Marissa — can you bring the kernel/quantization trade-off slide from our optimize pack?

-Rafael
